principles: Extend the existing trend-based detector into a block/allow gate — one stall-decision surface, never a parallel detector.
Block at the review-round mint site; the block clears ONLY by a recorded, signed, current-round structured resolution.
Keep the block decision a pure function of observable state (round count + per-round blocking trend + presence of a current-round resolution); I/O stays in the handler/gate.
Coexist independently with the advance-counting convergence-breaker — separate accounting, separate clear paths, no double-count.
Surface ill-posedness early: the declare-unreachable hatch (and plan/claim reconciliation) is the point, not a raw numeric cap.
drivers: F-058: it took 12 review rounds to discover a checklist item was unreachable; a raw cap would have stopped the spin but never surfaced the unreachability.
F-059: plan.md claimed delivery from round 4 and was never reconciled — the resolution action must force reconciliation.
Today the stall signal is advisory-only and was ignored for 20+ rounds.
convergence-breaker counts ADVANCES (maxAdvance=20) and never bit on review-round runaway (14 finding-bearing rounds passed under it).

options.name: A: block at REVIEW re-entry via a new pure gate in review-convergence.ts + a signed stall-adjudication record with an action enum + hard ceiling/override + independent breaker coexistence
pros: Blocks where the advisory already lives and where the round is minted
Reuses the existing trend detector (no false-cap on converging stories)
One structured-resolution surface incl. the unreachable hatch
cons: Touches the REVIEW transition guard (state-machine change)
Needs a new persisted+signed record + CLI

options.name: B: block at review_run_start instead
pros: Closer to the literal per-run mint
cons: review_run_start is per-reviewer-lane, not per-round — conflates lane starts with round mints
The advisory and round increment live at REVIEW entry, so the gate would be split from its signal
Harder to reason about clear semantics

options.name: C: just make convergence-breaker count review rounds / lower maxAdvance
cons: Conflates two accounting domains and risks double-count/regression
A raw cap never surfaces unreachability (fails the F-058 acceptance)

chosen: A: block at REVIEW re-entry via a new pure gate in review-convergence.ts + a signed stall-adjudication record with an action enum + hard ceiling/override + independent breaker coexistence
rationale: A blocks at the same site the advisory already lives (REVIEW re-entry / round mint), extends the existing pure trend detector into a block/allow gate so a genuinely converging story is never falsely capped, adds the signed structured-resolution record (including the declare-unreachable hatch that reconciles plan/claims per F-059) that alone clears the block, and keeps the advance-counting breaker on its own counter and story_resume --ack path. B misplaces the gate at per-lane granularity and splits it from its signal; C conflates the two accounting domains, cannot surface unreachability, and omits the resolution hatch — failing the acceptance criteria.

preMortem.scenario: The block fires on a HEALTHY converging story and stops legitimate progress
preMortem.trigger: the stall gate uses a raw round ceiling instead of the trend
preMortem.consequence: legitimate review rounds are refused, harming throughput
preMortem.mitigation: reuse the EXISTING trend-based assessReviewConvergence decision (already excludes trailing-clean last==0 and strictly-decreasing windows — not a raw cap); the RED smoke asserts a converging/decreasing-blocker trend is NOT blocked at or beyond STALL_MIN_ROUNDS

preMortem.scenario: Double-count / clear-path collision with the advance-counting convergence-breaker
preMortem.trigger: the new gate shares the breaker advance counter or is cleared by story_resume --ack
preMortem.consequence: both brakes freeze together, or --ack wrongly clears the stall block (or vice-versa)
preMortem.mitigation: key the stall adjudication on resolveReviewRoundCount with its OWN signed clear record (stall_resolution_set), independent of advanceBaseline/story_resume --ack; the smoke drives each brake to its own trigger and asserts the other neither fires nor clears

preMortem.scenario: The block is trivially bypassable by re-recording an empty resolution every round — the gate becomes theater
preMortem.trigger: a resolution record is accepted without substance or without binding to the current stalled round
preMortem.consequence: unlimited rounds continue, defeating the purpose
preMortem.mitigation: require a signed resolution with a reason (min length) bound to the CURRENT stalled review round (a previous-round record does not clear the current block), and a hard ceiling that caps total ordinary rounds even with resolutions unless a privileged override with its own reason is recorded

preMortem.scenario: declare-unreachable closes the loop but plan.md/claims still assert delivery — F-059 drift recurs
preMortem.trigger: the unreachable action does not reconcile the plan/claims
preMortem.consequence: the exact plan-vs-evidence drift the story targets happens again
preMortem.mitigation: the unreachable action marks the checklist item withdrawn/unreachable using B-1909 withdrawn-disposition semantics and requires the plan/claim reconciliation; the smoke asserts the declared item is marked withdrawn and the loop closes rather than minting another round
